channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: 6 dead, 15 injured in market square shooting in Poland: Police
item.description: Six people were killed and several others injured after shots were fired in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday, according to regional police.

item.title: 'A violent fighter and warrior': Trump offers press secretary role to UFC chief Dana White
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Saturday said he was asking mixed martial arts promoter Dana White to be the new White House press secretary. Trump has repeatedly tried to hitch his MAGA brand of politics to White's enormously successful Ultimate Fighting Championship.

item.title: Israel's president taps opposition candidate, not Netanyahu, to form a government
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot ran as the main rival to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but neither won enough support to command a majority. Israel's main parties have recommended Eisenkot form a new government.

item.title: Blow for Netanyahu as opposition rival asked to form government by Israel's president
item.description: Israel's president has asked Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, Gadi Eisenkot, to try and form a government following a deadlocked election.

item.title: France Unbowed’s Mélenchon unveils ‘A Shared Future’ manifesto ahead of 2027 presidential race
item.description: “We are facing a crisis of human civilisation. And we are going to win.” A defiant Jean-Luc Mélenchon was in fighting mood today as he presented his presidential manifesto at Le Bourget, north of Paris. It is his fourth bid for the French presidency, and he has chosen a venue steeped in left-wing campaign history: the site of François Hollande's famous 2012 rally.

item.title: Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot to try to form government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog picked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to try to form a government, he said in a statement Saturday. Last month's parliamentary elections left neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a clear path to building a majority.

item.title: Gunman opens fire in Polish city of Krakow, killing 6 people and injuring 15
item.description: A gunman targeted random people as he drove into Krakow's Main Square, a major tourist spot. Police shot and wounded the gunman during a gunfight.

item.title: Suspect arrested in connection with NYC jogger's murder: Police
item.description: The NYPD arrested a man on Saturday in connection with the killing of Katie Suarez, who was stabbed while jogging in Brooklyn last week.

item.title: 'We must change everything': French far-left leader Mélenchon launches presidential programme
item.description: Veteran leftist Jean-Luc Mélenchon formally announced his plan to raise France's minimum wage, cap prices for essential foods and restore the country's retirement age to 60 in a speech launching his 2027 presidential election programme on Saturday. Polls currently indicate that he is the left wing's strongest contender against far-right candidate Marine Le Pen.

item.title: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.

item.title: France investigating if bogus bomb threats against airlines linked to 'foreign powers'
item.description: French prosecutors are investigating a series of fake bomb threats that targeted commercial flights in Europe this week, including trying to establish whether foreign powers may be involved. Those responsible for the bogus threats have not been identified.

item.title: Gunman who killed at least six people in Krakow had ‘far-right’ views, Polish government says
item.description: A gunman reportedly "fascinated by far-right ideologies" shot and killed at least six people and wounded more than a dozen more in Krakow’s main market square on Saturday, Polish authorities said. Three more bodies were later found at the home of the gunman, who was wounded and taken into custody.

item.title: Travel delays feared as fog warning issued for parts of England
item.description: Thick fog could lead to travel disruption across much of England from midnight on Saturday to late Sunday morning, the Met Office has warned.

item.title: WATCH: Firefighters give kids a superhero surprise
item.description: Corpus Christi firefighters dressed as superheroes surprised patients at Driscoll Children's Hospital by rappelling down the glass building as kids waved.

item.title: Pope Leo calls on Uruguay's Catholics to be 'bridge builders'
item.description: Pope Leo XIV urged Catholics in Uruguay to build bridges of faith and fraternity on the second day of his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. The pope's three-country tour comes just three weeks after he underwent surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: A promising new medicine against heart disease fails unexpectedly
item.description: Doctors expected an experimental drug that lowers a common risk factor for heart attacks would save patients' lives. The medicine made no difference.

item.title: 'We must change everything,' French far-left presidential candidate Mélenchon says
item.description: Veteran leftist Jean-Luc Mélenchon formally announced his plan to raise France's minimum wage, cap prices for essential foods and restore the country's retirement age to 60 in a speech launching his 2027 presidential election programme on Saturday. Polls currently indicate that he is the left wing's strongest contender against far-right candidate Marine Le Pen.

item.title: At least 27 people killed in strike near Yemen's capital, Houthi official says
item.description: At least 27 people have been killed and 36 others wounded, mostly women and children, after airstrikes hit homes in a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, a spokesman for Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry said.

item.title: Two teenagers arrested after boys chased with sword in Gloucester
item.description: Two teenagers have been arrested after a boy was attacked with a sword in Tuffley, police said.

item.title: France braces for more nationwide protests as Yellow Vests urge 'mass disobedience'
item.description: French unions and student groups are set to take to the streets for another day of protests on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities. The demonstrations follow weeks of youth-led unrest and nationwide strikes that drew hundreds of thousands of workers protesting over the rising cost of living. Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French history and politics at the University of Nottingham, and James André, France 24 reporter at Place de la République, share further insights.

item.title: Nations League: Zinedine Zidane balances surprise and continuity in his second roster
item.description: Zinedine Zidane has unveiled his France squad for the upcoming Nations League clashes against Italy and Turkey. Pablo Pagis earns a surprise first call-up, while Kylian Mbappé and several other key players return from injury

item.title: Democrats plan to widen their probes of fatal ICE shootings
item.description: The killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti during the ICE surge in Minneapolis last winter was a pivotal moment for the country. After Democrats' sweeping wins this week, their deaths at the hands of immigration agents will likely be the targets of renewed investigations.

item.title: Perspective: Simon Winchester was here to tell a story
item.description: British American reporter and author Simon Winchester died of a heart attack Nov. 3. We take a moment to remember his long career, which included covering Bloody Sunday and Watergate.

item.title: No clear winner after New Zealand general election
item.description: The New Zealand election count has ended without a definitive result as the two main parties remain almost deadlocked in the popular vote.

item.title: Banking scandal topples Paraguay leader
item.description: Paraguay’s ousted president Santiago Peña has been placed under house arrest after senators unanimously voted to remove him over a banking scandal. The collapse of Ueno Bank left nearly three million customers unable to access their savings. Peña denies any wrongdoing, while his successor, Pedro Alliana, has pledged to compensate those affected.

item.title: Russia launches massive strike on Kyiv
item.description: As Ukraine prepares for another round of talks with Russia and the United States next week, Moscow has launched a massive overnight strike. At least five people were injured in Kyiv, where Russian missiles damaged residential and commercial buildings, forced the closure of a bridge over the Dnipro River and caused fresh power and water outages. Ophélie Jacobson reports.

item.title: Stephen Miller named White House Chief of Staff
item.description: Following historic Republican losses in the midterm elections, Donald Trump has replaced his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with her deputy Stephen Miller, the architect of his administration’s immigration crackdown. Wiles had been seen by some as a stabilising force in the White House, but with Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, Trump is reportedly seeking a more aggressive approach to pushing his agenda. Caroline Baum reports.

item.title: Israel coalition talks gain momentum
item.description: Following inconclusive elections in Israel, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot says he is confident of securing the mandate to form a government, as President Isaac Herzog prepares to nominate the first candidate. Eisenkot claims he is making progress in efforts to oust long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison
item.description: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the deaths of 190 children who were starved to death on his orders in Shakahola Forest. Prosecutors said he had convinced followers to fast to reach heaven before the apocalypse, with some victims beaten, buried alive or dumped in latrines. Twenty-eight accomplices have also been jailed. The case has raised serious questions about the authorities' failure to act on repeated warning signs dating back to 2017, with the death toll from the wider investigation reaching 448 confirmed bodies and around 500 suspected victims.

item.title: Retired tennis star Gaël Monfils named captain of France's Davis Cup team
item.description: Recently retired tennis player Gaël Monfils was named captain of the French Davis Cup team, the country's tennis federation announced Saturday. France will next take part in the Davis Cup in February 2027 after having failed to qualify for this year's finals in Bologna.

item.title: Thousands turn out to greet Pope Leo as he begins Latin America tour
item.description: Thousands of people greeted Pope Leo as he arrived in Uruguay at the start of a 12-day tour of Latin America.

item.title: This teen boy set out to get people talking about periods. He's now a Diana honoree
item.description: This year's the Princess Diana honor roll highlights 198 inspiring young activists and advocates — including an 18-year-old guy in India who founded Team Period.

item.title: French presidential election: How far-left Mélenchon became a Gen Z favourite
item.description: Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon presents his policy platform at a key rally near Paris on Saturday. A polarising figure for the general electorate, he is nonetheless beloved among France's youth, who are drawn to his progressive policy proposals and say he empowers them to get more involved in politics.

item.title: An unexpected activist emerged to help block a $5 billion data center in Maryland
item.description: Thousands across the U.S. have gotten involved to oppose data centers. One is a Maryland woman who'd been evicted after a pay cut and became a leader of a community effort that blocked a vast project.

item.title: Pope urges healthcare for all in Uruguay
item.description: Three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, Pope Francis has begun a three-nation tour of Latin America, saying he felt better than he looked. His first stop is Uruguay, the continent’s most secular country. Jack Pownall reports.

item.title: AI Data centres face growing backlash
item.description: Democrats are also calling for tighter regulation of AI data centres, a concern shared across Europe. In Amsterdam, several hundred activists occupied the site of a planned Microsoft data centre as part of a two-day protest taking place across the continent. Jennie Shin reports.

item.title: Yemen: 30 dead in strikes on Taiz market
item.description: At least 30 people have reportedly been killed in an attack on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province, with Houthi rebels blaming Saudi airstrikes. Government forces and local authorities have disputed the claim, instead accusing the Houthis of indiscriminate fire. The province has witnessed intense clashes in recent weeks and is home to around half of the more than 300,000 people displaced by the latest fighting. Caroline Baum reports.

item.title: USA: Democrats vow to investigate Donald Trump
item.description: In this new era of divided government, Democratic lawmakers say their priorities will be tackling the rising cost of living, investigating alleged corruption and tightening oversight of ICE agents. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

item.title: French student unions say 250,000 people took part in Saturday’s protests
item.description: Roughly 250,000 people took part in Saturday’s country-wide demonstrations against the rising cost of living and in support of the ongoing youth movement, a group of French student unions said. The Interior Ministry put the number at closer to 146,000. Follow our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Meghan's father in court charged with possessing child abuse material
item.description: The Duchess of Sussex's father has appeared in court after being arrested and charged with allegedly possessing child sexual abuse images.

item.title: Democrats flip statehouses in midterm wave
item.description: The showing across the country that flipped Congress to Democratic control on Election Day also trickled down to the state and local level.

item.title: UK has 'new pair of eyes' in space as new military satellite enters orbit
item.description: The UK has a "new pair of eyes" in space after it launched a new military satellite into orbit, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) has announced.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed's grandparents reflect on his historic Senate win
item.description: Judy and Jan Johnson spoke with ABC News Live about how proud they are to see their grandson, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, be elected to Senate.

item.title: Man appears in court charged with murder of missing woman
item.description: A man has appeared in court charged with the murder of a missing woman whose whereabouts remain unknown.

item.title: Trump says chief of staff Susie Wiles out, Stephen Miller will replace her
item.description: Trump said his top aide Stephen Miller will replace her in the job.

item.title: Latino vote helped thwart Texas Republicans' redistricting effort
item.description: Last year, the Republican-controlled Texas legislature redrew its congressional maps aimed at giving the GOP five more seats.

item.title: WATCH: Guide dog Eddie named 2026 American Humane Society Hero Dog
item.description: Eddie, a 3-year-old Labrador retriever, was honored for changing the life of his legally blind owner, Luis Rodriguez, through his work as a guide dog.

item.title: Deep forces are reshaping America's electoral map - and what it means for White House race
item.description: This week's American midterm was a once-in-a-lifetime result.

item.title: US attorney tasked with leading probe into Trump's foes resigns from DOJ
item.description: Jason Reding Quinones, the U.S. attorney tasked with leading a sweeping and controversial conspiracy probe targeting President Trump’s foes, has resigned from the DOJ.

item.title: The economy propelled Democrats to victory. What can they actually do about it?
item.description: The party's success was fueled by frustrations over the cost of living. But in divided government, they'll face opposition from Republicans in Congress and a president vowing to use his veto pen.

item.title: WATCH: $11.4M shipment of Nvidia cargo stolen from Oakland
item.description: Experts describe the computer hardware theft as a sophisticated cargo heist.

item.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
item.description: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key.

item.title: WATCH: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s grandparents react to historic win in Michigan
item.description: Jan and Judy Johnson, grandparents of Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, join ABC News Live to reflect on his Senate victory, their blended interfaith family and the traditions that bring them together.

item.title: Boy, 6, dies in hospital after house fire that killed four members of his family
item.description: A six-year-old who sustained critical injuries during a house fire that killed four members of his family has also died, police said.

item.title: Connecticut Sen. Murphy discharged from hospital after stroke, goes to rehab facility
item.description: Connecticut Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy says he has been discharged from the hospital after suffering a stroke last weekend and will miss “several weeks” of votes in the Senate as he recovers in a rehabilitation facility

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Fall’s beautiful colors on display at Utah’s Zion National Park
item.description: You can see more about Zion and other national parks on "National Parks USA," streaming now on Disney+.

item.title: WATCH: 1st look at Nat Geo's 'Wolves Up Close with Bertie Gregory'
item.description: The new National Geographic documentary follows Bertie Gregory to Canada's Hudson Bay as he captures rare wolf behaviors during the harsh Arctic winter.

item.title: US officials unveil $280K deal to help Puerto Rico face water and power crises
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has met with nonprofits in Puerto Rico as officials announced a $280,000 partnership to help the U.S. territory confront emergencies

item.title: Trump moves to make Oval Office a national monument to prevent future major changes
item.description: Trump indicated the proclamation would have to be ratified by Congress.

item.title: Jay Rockefeller, former West Virginia governor and US senator, dies at 89
item.description: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family’s political dynasty who served as West Virginia’s governor and later a longtime U.S. senator, has died

item.title: Election 2026 live results: Raman promises smooth transition of power to LA mayor
item.description: Raman is poised to become the 44th mayor of the nation’s second-largest city.

item.title: Two dead after bus carrying schoolchildren crashes in France, officials say
item.description: A seven-year-old girl and an 18-year-old boy have been killed after a bus crashed in eastern France, French authorities said.

item.title: WATCH: Multiple water rescues amid flood emergencies in the South
item.description: A flood emergency is underway across multiple states in the South – triggering dozens of water rescues in Florida, Georgia and Tennessee in the middle of the night.

item.title: WATCH: These identical twin sisters speak at the same time
item.description: Danny New talks to identical twin sisters in Australia who are turning heads for their unique speech patterns.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities reveal motive in Citibank complex shooting
item.description: Chilling surveillance video shows a gunman exchanging gunfire with a security guard after ramming a gate at a Citibank complex near Tampa and killing a woman having lunch, authorities say.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the man who's the new voice of Boston's Logan airport
item.description: Christopher Donisi, an HVAC pipe fitter, will be the man behind the first voice travelers hear when they land in Beantown in the near future.

item.title: WATCH: Jaguars face injury-ravaged Ravens in Thursday Night Football matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler previews the Jaguars-Ravens matchup, Baltimore’s quarterback injuries and Trevor Lawrence’s strong start to the season.

item.title: WATCH: Bob Dylan, Prince William, Prince Harry: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC News' Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including Bob Dylan meeting with Pope Leo at the Vatican and Prince William and Prince Harry joining forces to honor their mother.
